And they set out early in the morning; the garden owners’ departure to carry out their plan.
Believing themselves able to carry out their plan; that belief did not guarantee obtaining the produce.

corrections: Preserved all 353 supplied blocks in each language, including all 19 derivative entries. Added complete English translation, 8 sections, 37 subheadings, 20 morphology cards, and transliterations for all 9 displayed Arabic quotations.
Corrected Al-Ashhab ibn Rumaylah from a simply Umayyad-era designation to mukhadram, following Khizanat al-Adab. His lifetime does not securely date the quoted verse.

Retained the defensible interpretation of al-asawid as brave men, but explained the alternative black-serpents interpretation recorded in Khizanat al-Adab. Removed weakness from the direct translation of Jarir’s haridan; its contextual explanation remains.
Clarified that the explicitly quoted withholding construction in Lisan is Form II harrada al-shay. Distinguished transitive harama (deprive someone) from passive deprivation and from hurmah/haram.

Clarified qadirin in context as the owners’ belief in their ability, following Tabari, rather than proof that they could actually obtain already-damaged produce. Preserved the supplied proposed verse rendering and clearly labeled all three article verse renderings as proposals.

Preserved the distinction between lexical purpose/resolve and the contextual intention to exclude the needy. Expanded abbreviated references to full Al-Qalam 68:24 references. Avoided claiming an early date for undated poetic witnesses.

Updated the own bilingual registry entry and the two unprotected hard word boxes in 68:25 from the exact article summary. Added two own contexts and four missing surrounding contexts; removed only the own obsolete preliminary notice. All three assigned roots match QAC.

Verified 8 bilingual verse targets and 10 related-study links. Preliminary related roots were left without article links. No authored reflection in the target verse in either language. Existing Arabic, verse translations, grammatical metadata, Fatihah, Baqarah through 160, root indexes, shared rendering, and prior work preserved.
Required focused root-box check passed before installation: six complete bilingual lexical boxes. No post-installation tests, build, preview, commit, or push.
